title: Bài sưu tầm 324 - Passage 3: The Paradox of Musical Prodigies
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 324

The Paradox of Musical Prodigies

Paragraph 1. Concert halls have long been captivated by the spectacle of an eight-year-old pianist effortlessly navigating a Chopin nocturne before an audience of seasoned critics. Yet historical surveys reveal an uncomfortable truth: very few child prodigies go on to reshape the musical landscape as adults. In Beyond Early Brilliance, musicologist Dr. Hannah Lindqvist examines why extraordinary juvenile mastery rarely translates into lasting artistic innovation. The answer, she argues, lies not in a sudden loss of talent, but in a sharp mismatch between the skills rewarded in childhood and those demanded in maturity.

Paragraph 2. Young prodigies excel primarily at faithful reproduction. Blessed with exceptional auditory memory and fine motor coordination, they absorb established scores rapidly and replicate the stylistic nuances of older masters with uncanny accuracy. Conservatories and international youth competitions reinforce this habit by awarding prizes for technical precision and fidelity to canonised recordings. However, as Lindqvist notes, imitation is fundamentally conservative: mastering the rules laid down by previous generations trains the young performer to avoid mistakes rather than take aesthetic risks.

Paragraph 3. The transition to adulthood confronts the former prodigy with an unsettling psychological shift. Audiences no longer applaud merely because a performer is young; the novelty of age evaporates, leaving behind a far sterner demand for an original artistic voice. Many celebrated child performers discover that decades of tightly scheduled practice—often orchestrated by ambitious parents or managers—have left them little room for unguided play, boredom, or personal experimentation. When asked to compose or interpret boldly without an instructor's blueprint, some experience acute creative paralysis, quietly retreating into teaching or routine orchestral work.

Paragraph 4. Conversely, biographies of revolutionary composers such as Ludwig van Beethoven or the jazz innovator Thelonious Monk tell a notably different story. Though unmistakably gifted, neither was celebrated as a polished, error-free child virtuoso; both showed stubborn eccentricities, resisted rigid drills, and spent years wandering across musical boundaries before producing mature breakthroughs. Crucially, Lindqvist warns educators against treating early fluency as a guarantee of future genius—or dismissing late-blooming adolescents whose messy curiosity resists neat competition rubrics. True artistic originality, she concludes, begins only when a musician dares to unlearn perfection.

q27.text: According to Dr. Hannah Lindqvist, why do few musical prodigies transform music in adulthood?
options: A. Their auditory memory deteriorates rapidly after adolescence.
B. The qualities that bring childhood success differ from those driving adult innovation.
C. Critics lose interest in classical repertoire once performers grow older.
D. Physical hand injuries from intense training end most solo careers.

steps: Đoạn 1: Không phải do mất tài năng, mà do sự lệch pha giữa kỹ năng được tán thưởng lúc nhỏ và kỹ năng cần ở tuổi trưởng thành.
Kết luận: Chọn B.

q28.text: In the second paragraph, the writer suggests that youth music competitions tend to
options: A. overlook performers with natural motor coordination.
B. encourage young pianists to compose experimental pieces.
C. penalize candidates who study older masters too closely.
D. reward error-free conformity over personal artistic risk.

steps: Đoạn 2: Các cuộc thi trao giải cho độ chính xác kỹ thuật và bám sát bản thu kinh điển, rèn cho người trẻ tránh lỗi thay vì mạo hiểm thẩm mỹ.
Kết luận: Chọn D.

q29.text: What problem do some prodigies face when their careers become self-directed?
options: A. Strict early routines have left them unprepared to generate original ideas.
B. Parents continue to block them from accepting orchestral appointments.
C. They are barred from teaching inside traditional conservatories.
D. Concert halls prefer booking younger performers on lower fees.

steps: Đoạn 3: Hàng thập kỷ tập luyện theo lịch ép sẵn khiến họ thiếu không gian thử nghiệm cá nhân; khi không còn khuôn mẫu của thầy, họ dễ rơi vào tê liệt sáng tạo.
Kết luận: Chọn A.
Đoạn 1: sharp mismatch between the skills rewarded in childhood and those demanded in maturity ↔ mismatch (F).
Đoạn 2: faithful reproduction / replicate the stylistic nuances ↔ accurate imitation (C).
Đoạn 2: avoid mistakes rather than take aesthetic risks ↔ technical caution (H).
Đoạn 3: without an instructor's blueprint ↔ creative autonomy (B).
Đoạn 4: resisted rigid drills ↔ strict early discipline (E).
Đoạn 4: dares to unlearn perfection ↔ accepting imperfection (A).

q36.text: Only a small minority of child prodigies later become groundbreaking adult musicians.

steps: Đoạn 1: "very few child prodigies go on to reshape the musical landscape as adults."
Kết luận: Chọn YES.

q37.text: Judges at international youth competitions are mostly retired orchestra conductors.

steps: Đoạn 2 (Bẫy từ khóa): Bài có nhắc international youth competitions và orchestral work (ở đoạn 3), nhưng hoàn toàn không đề cập thành phần ban giám khảo các cuộc thi trẻ là ai.
Kết luận: Chọn NOT GIVEN.

q38.text: Adult audiences evaluate mature performers with the same leniency shown to young prodigies.

steps: Đoạn 3: Sự mới lạ của tuổi tác biến mất, nhường chỗ cho đòi hỏi khắt khe hơn nhiều về dấu ấn nghệ thuật riêng (leaving behind a far sterner demand).
Kết luận: Chọn NO.

q39.text: Educators should avoid assuming that awkward, unpolished teenagers lack major creative potential.

steps: Đoạn 4: Lindqvist cảnh báo không nên gạt bỏ những thiếu niên nở muộn có sự tò mò lộn xộn không vừa khuôn điểm thi (dismissing late-blooming adolescents whose messy curiosity resists neat competition rubrics).
Kết luận: Chọn YES.

q40.text: Which subtitle best summarizes the central idea of Reading Passage 324?
options: A. Why modern conservatories are abolishing competitive music exams
B. How childhood auditory memory determines lifelong compositional talent
C. Why early technical perfection can hinder mature musical originality
D. The financial pressures placed on child performers by concert halls

steps: Chủ đề xuyên suốt: Sự hoàn hảo kỹ thuật sớm dựa trên bắt chước dễ kìm hãm tính nguyên bản sáng tạo ở tuổi trưởng thành.
Kết luận: Chọn C.
